events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.92)
events.body: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip, so the fee can only stand if NS-1 is fully satisfied via NS-0 [F3][NS-0]. NS-1 has three cumulative preconditions: an "I'm Here" press, GPS placing the driver at the pickup, and waiting there over 3 minutes [NS-1]. The system records show the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 545 m and he never entered 200 m at any point, and the platform never recorded an arrival [F1][F4][NS-1]. At the moment of the 12:05:55 tap he was 601 m away and spent 0 s inside the arrival radius afterwards, and his only stationary period (12:05:35–12:09:05, 3 min 30 s) was served 600 m from the pickup [F5][F2][NS-1]. Both NS-1(ii) and NS-1(iii) therefore fail, and the driver's statement that he pressed the button and waited at the pickup is contradicted by these records; system records (gps/timeline/fare) govern over statements such as F12 and the chat messages F9/F11 [F12][F9][F11][F1][F2][NS-1]. The rider's chat at 12:06 placing herself at the pickup point is consistent with the GPS record, so there is no evidence of rider no-show [F10][F1][NS-2]. Because NS-1 fails, the $6.61 cancellation fee does not stand and is refunded in full [F3][F7][NS-2]. The amount is the recorded cancellation fee of $6.61 with a 1.0× surge multiplier (no surge scaling applies) [F7][F8][NS-2]. The fee is refundable as a Ryde voucher rather than cash, and the filing is timely [F3][F7][NS-7]. Separately, the driver tapped "I'm Here" while 601 m from the pickup with 0 s inside the arrival radius, which is abuse of the arrival button and calls for an account flag in addition to the refund [F5][F1][NS-2]. The F5/F6 inconsistency (a tap recorded at 12:05:55 versus a null driver_pressed_here_at) does not change the outcome either way, because both readings place the driver 545–601 m from the pickup [F5][F6][F1][NS-1]. The driver's clean 90-day record (0 disputes, 0 upheld over 502 trips) is a profile fact and cannot alone decide the case; it does not remove the flag triggered by the false arrival tap [F17][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; record the false "I'm Here" tap against the driver's account for Ryde review; no refund of cash.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest GPS approach was 545 m away at 12:05:20 and he was never within 200 m at any time, so the NS-1 requirement that he be at the pickup location is not met.
When the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:05:55 the platform recorded him 601 m from the pickup point and he stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds afterwards, so the NS-1 'arrived' precondition is false.

System records also show no "I'm Here" event at all (driver_pressed_here_at is null) and no recorded arrival (driver_arrived_at is null), so the driver's own statement that he pressed the button and waited at the pickup cannot be reconciled with the platform records.

The driver's only stationary period, 12:05:35–12:09:05 (3 min 30 s), was spent 600 m from the pickup point, not at the pickup point, so even the elapsed-time element of NS-1(iii) was served in the wrong place.

The rider confirmed in chat at 12:06 that she was at the pickup point and could not see the driver's car, and the driver cancelled at 12:08–12:09 without ever coming to her, so the rider did not fail to show up.
Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) are each unmet, the $6.61 cancellation fee recorded on the trip must be refunded in full to the rider under NS-2.

The driver's conduct matches Ryde's listed abuse of the arrival/cancellation button (tapping 'I'm Here' while not at the pickup point), which NS-2 makes grounds for an account flag in addition to the refund.
The request is timely: the trip was cancelled at 12:09:05 on the trip date and this dispute is filed within the 30-day window of NS-7, so the $6.61 refund is payable as a Ryde voucher.

Even if the driver never reached the pickup point, he did remain stationary for 3 min 30 s (F2), which the other side may present as a genuine attempt to wait rather than button abuse, weakening the flag_account request (F17 also shows 0 prior upheld disputes).

claims.assertion: The driver's GPS track never placed him at the pickup point: his closest approach was 545 m at 12:05:20 and he never came within 200 m of Bugis Junction, so NS-1(ii) (GPS showing the driver at the pickup point) is not satisfied.

The driver's only stationary period was 12:05:35–12:09:05 (3 min 30 s) spent 600 m away from the pickup point, so any waiting occurred outside the pickup location and outside the 200 m arrival radius required by NS-1(ii).

The driver's own written statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited over 3 minutes at the pickup is contradicted by the system records: he pressed the button 601 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds afterwards, so the system record governs and NS-1(i)–(iii) fails.

The chat log confirms the rider was at the pickup point and could not see the car, and the driver's own 12:06 message placed him "here" while the GPS shows he was still 545–600 m away; the rider's account matches the GPS record rather than the driver's statement.

Because NS-1 is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand and must be refunded in full to the rider under NS-2; the fee amount on record is $6.61 with no surge multiplier, so the refund is exactly $6.61.

No mitigating reroute or traffic justification exists for the driver's absence from the pickup point: there were no speed-band records and no traffic incidents on the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

The driver's 90-day record shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes over 502 trips, so the mis-tap appears to be an isolated incident rather than a pattern warranting an account-level sanction; no flag_account is sought against the driver on this record.

weaknesses: F6 records that driver_pressed_here_at is null, while F5 records an "I'm Here" tap at 12:05:55; the rider will cite F6 to argue the driver never marked arrival at all, which only strengthens the rider's NS-1(i) failure claim.

The driver did tap "I'm Here" while 601 m from the pickup (F5), which on its face supports the rider's abuse-of-arrival-button argument under NS-2 read with the fraud-listing provisions, and my case cannot explain why he tapped while still ~600 m away.

The driver's chat message "I'm here already" at 12:06 (F9) is contradicted by GPS (F1, F2), and I have no system fact showing he was delayed by traffic or road closure — F13–F15 show no such cause — so he has no defensible excuse for being 545–600 m away.
His 3 min 30 s stationary period (F2) was spent 600 m from the pickup, so even the locally generous reading of the waiting requirement cannot satisfy NS-1(iii) at the pickup point.

The internal conflict between F5 (a tap at 12:05:55) and F6 (driver_pressed_here_at null) means the null value cannot be treated as affirmative proof that no button was ever pressed, and in any event both readings fail NS-1(ii) because F1/F5 place him 545–601 m away, so no finding should rest on the null field.
Conceded: F2 shows the only stationary period of 3 min 30 s (12:05:35–12:09:05) was spent 600 m from the pickup, so the elapsed-time element of NS-1(iii) was served away from the pickup point.

The rider's chat message F10 and the driver's own messages F9/F11 are statements that must yield to the GPS record F1/F2, which shows the driver was 545–600 m away the whole time; the rider's position therefore agrees with the system record, and no evidence shows the rider failed to appear.

The flag_account request should be refused: F17 shows 502 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes, and F2 shows a genuine 3 min 30 s stationery wait, so this is an isolated wrong-location arrival rather than the repeated or severe conduct RD-6 requires; the F5/F6 conflict also means the button event itself is not reliably established.
